title: Implementation of orbitrap mass spectrometry for improved GC-MS target analysis in lithium ion battery electrolytes
author: Peschel, Horsthemke, et al.
materials: GC-HRMS investigations were performed on a Q Exactive GC Orbitrap GC-MS/MS system with a TRACE 1310 GC and a TriPlus RSH autosampler (all Thermo Fisher Scientific, USA). The Q Exactive GC setup control was carried out by means of Xcalibur 4.2 SP1 (Thermo Fisher).

GC separation was performed on a nonpolar Supelco SLB-5ms (30 m × 0.25 mm; 0.25 μm) column (Sigma Aldrich, Germany). Helium 6.0 (Westfalen, Germany) was used as carrier gas in constant column flow mode, set at 1.16 mL min−1. The temperature program started at 40 °C, which was held for 1 min followed by ramps of 3 °C min−1 up to 60 °C and 30 °C up to 260 °C. The final temperature was held for 2 min. Transferlines to the Q Exactive system were operated at 250 °C.

Data analysis like chromatogram extraction and mass peak resolution determination was performed with FreeStyle 1.5 (Thermo Fisher). EICs were extracted from Full MS experiments based on measured m/z values with a mass window of 5 ppm. Chromatograms and spectra were plotted with OriginPro 2019b (OriginLab, USA).

In addition to the exemplarily discussed and targeted butyl carbonates, further methyl and ethyl carbonate-based structures were identified in the considered retention time window. These were also identified in previous studies as methyl propyl carbonate (MPC) and ethyl propyl carbonate (EPC) [2]. On the one hand, this findings illustrate the applicability of carbonate marker fragment ions not only for targeted analysis of the aimed species, but also for screening of unknown mixtures. Marker fragment ions simplify identification of further species that could contain similar substructures. On the other hand, the fast identification of further species demonstrates, that more general target lists for a majority of literature known carbonate-based decomposition species are hardly achievable. Due to structural similarities of species containing mainly carbonate, glycol and alkyl moieties, fragmentation of larger (oligomeric) species results in the same “marker” fragment ions. Furthermore, EI fragmentation pathways can be very complex and uncharacteristic towards molecule ion structures e.g. due to rearrangements. Nevertheless, screening with EICs of marker fragment ions can also be considered for fast sample screening in non-targeted approaches.

steps.title: Set up GC‑Orbitrap system
steps.instruction: Install and power the Q Exactive GC Orbitrap GC‑MS/MS equipped with a TRACE 1310 GC and a TriPlus RSH autosampler (Thermo Fisher Scientific, USA). Control the instrument using Xcalibur version 4.2 SP1 (Thermo Fisher).

steps.title: Prepare injection port and sample introduction
steps.instruction: Set the injection port temperature to 250 °C and operate in split mode with a 1:100 split ratio for liquid injections and 1:10 for solid‑phase microextraction (SPME). For liquid injection, draw 1 µL of sample with a 10 µL syringe and inject. For SPME, manually expose the fiber to the headspace of a 20 mL vial for 10 min at room temperature, then desorb the analytes in the injector at 250 °C for 60 s. Before each sample, condition the SPME fiber at 260 °C for 300 s and run a blank of ambient air to check for carry‑over.

steps.title: Configure GC column and temperature program
steps.instruction: Install a non‑polar Supelco SLB‑5ms column (30 m × 0.25 mm, 0.25 µm film). Use Helium 6.0 (Westfalen, Germany) as carrier gas in constant flow mode set to 1.16 mL min⁻¹. Program the oven: start at 40 °C, hold 1 min; ramp at 3 °C min⁻¹ to 60 °C; then ramp at 30 °C min⁻¹ to 260 °C and hold for 2 min. Keep transfer lines to the Q Exactive at 250 °C.

steps.title: Set MS ionization and acquisition parameters
steps.instruction: Select electron‑impact (EI) ionization with 70 eV electron energy (auto‑tuned for TIC). Operate the mass spectrometer in Full MS mode, positive polarity, at a resolution of 60 000 FWHM at m/z 200. Set the automatic gain control target to 1 × 10⁶ and the maximum injection time to auto. Scan the mass range m/z 35–500 and record spectra in profile mode. Apply a solvent‑cut delay for filament and MS detection when highly concentrated solvent elutes at low retention times.

steps.title: Process data and extract ion chromatograms
steps.instruction: Analyze the data with Thermo Fisher FreeStyle 1.5. Extract extracted ion chromatograms (EICs) using the exact m/z values of target fragments with a mass window of 5 ppm. Plot chromatograms and spectra using OriginPro 2019b (OriginLab, USA).
